value: Oklahoma Consumer Data Privacy Act (Senate Bill 546, 2026 Okla. Sess. Laws ch. 8; 75A O.S. ss. 300-320)
Oklahoma Attorney General
Oklahoma residents acting in an individual or household context (not commercial or employment context)

Businesses operating in Oklahoma or targeting Oklahoma residents that process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers per year, or at least 25,000 consumers while deriving over 50% of gross revenue from selling personal data (75A O.S. s. 314(A))

Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port, and opt out of targeted advertising, sale and certain profiling (45-day response plus 45-day extension; appeal process); opt-in consent for sensitive data; privacy notices, data minimization and data protection assessments
Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data used to identify a person, precise geolocation); pseudonymous data
No fixed period; collection limited to what is reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes (data minimization); no specific retention schedule found
Oklahoma Attorney General (exclusive enforcement; no private right of action)
Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation after a 30-day cure period (non-sunsetting); injunction, attorney fees and investigation costs
State agencies and political subdivisions, nonprofits, institutions of higher education, HIPAA covered entities and data, GLBA financial institutions/data; employment and commercial contexts

Enrolled text on oklegislature.gov was not seen; dates and details come from law-firm summaries. Sources disagree on whether Oklahoma is the 20th or 21st state.
Not covered in sources found: consumer defined as an Oklahoma natural person acting in an individual or household context; no deceased-person provision found
Identifiable private information used in human subjects research is exempt; public-interest research permitted as a common business activity (section number not found)
Genetic or biometric data used to identify a person is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent before processing
Alabama Personal Data Protection Act (House Bill 351, Act 2026-552)
Alabama Attorney General
Alabama residents (consumers acting in an individual or household context)

Persons doing business in Alabama or targeting Alabama residents that process personal data of more than 25,000 consumers (excluding payment-only data) or derive more than 25% of gross revenue from selling personal data; businesses under 500 employees and nonprofits under 100 employees exempt unless they sell data
Consumer rights to confirm, correct, delete and opt out; sensitive data consent; secure channels to exercise rights; Virginia-style model but no mandatory data protection assessments
Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data used to identify an individual)
UNKNOWN
Alabama Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action)
Civil penalty up to $15,000 per violation; 45-day cure period that does not sunset

GLBA and HIPAA entities/data, small businesses under 500 employees and nonprofits under 100 employees (if not selling data), human subjects research data, patient safety work product (non-exhaustive list)

Louisiana Data Privacy Act (Senate Bill 386, Act No. 502 of 2026; La. R.S. 51:1780.1-1780.5)
Louisiana Attorney General
Louisiana residents acting in an individual or household capacity (not commercial or employment context)

Persons doing business in Louisiana meeting one of: annual gross revenue over $25 million; buying/selling/sharing personal information of 75,000+ consumers, households or devices; or 50%+ of revenue from selling personal information
Texas-style model: consumer rights (access, correct, delete, port, opt out); consent for sensitive data; data minimization, security and risk assessments
Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data)
UNKNOWN
Louisiana Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action)

No penalty schedule in the Act itself; violations are unfair trade practices under LUTPA, civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation (R.S. 51:1407) reported, higher where elderly or disabled persons affected; cure period only 2027-01-01 to 2027-07-31 (30-day notice)

State agencies and political subdivisions, GLBA financial institutions and data, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits, higher education institutions, public utilities; certain research data

Vermont Data Privacy and Online Surveillance Act (S.71, Act 145 of 2026; 9 V.S.A. ch. 61A, ss. 2415a-2415k)
Vermont Attorney General
Vermont residents (consumers); consumer health data provisions apply regardless of volume thresholds

Entities doing business in Vermont or targeting Vermont residents that process personal data of 35,000+ consumers or sensitive data of 3,000+ consumers or sell data of 3,000+ consumers; consumer health data rules apply without thresholds

Connecticut-style model: consumer rights; consent for sensitive data (incl. genetic, biometric, neural, precise geolocation, consumer health, known child data) and limits to what is reasonably necessary; privacy notices must disclose LLM training use; bans manipulative design; no sale or targeted ads for ages 13-17
Personal data; sensitive data (genetic, biometric, neural, precise geolocation, consumer health data, known child data)
UNKNOWN
Vermont Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action) under the Vermont Consumer Protection Act
Up to $10,000 per violation under the Consumer Protection Act; discretionary 60-day cure period 2028-01-01 to 2029-06-30
Data-level exemptions: various health data, GLBA data, FCRA data, emergency contact information, post-secondary school enrollment/degree verification and related research services

Florida Digital Bill of Rights (CS/CS/SB 262 'Technology Transparency', Ch. 2023-201, Laws of Fla.; Fla. Stat. ss. 501.701 et seq.)
Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Office of the Attorney General)
Florida residents (consumers); narrow controller definition so applies to few businesses

Controllers with over $1 billion global gross annual revenue that also derive 50%+ of revenue from online ad sales, operate a consumer smart speaker with voice assistant, or operate an app store with 250,000+ apps; some duties (e.g. sale of sensitive data) reach other for-profit businesses (s. 501.715)

Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out of sale, targeted ads and profiling; opt-in consent for sensitive data and its sale; data minimization, security and retention schedule; children's online protections
Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic data processed to uniquely identify, health diagnoses, precise geolocation)
Controllers and processors must adopt and follow a retention schedule; retention ends at the first of several triggers, including two years after the consumer's last interaction
Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General); no private right of action

Civil penalty up to $50,000 per violation, tripled (up to $150,000) for violations involving a child, failure to delete/correct after verified request, or continued sale/sharing after opt-out; discretionary 45-day cure period (not granted for child-related violations)
Entities below the $1 billion/prong thresholds; HIPAA and GLBA entities/data; research and other listed processing purposes (sections not confirmed)
